---
title: "Effects"
subtitle: "How do we measure effects and how do we interpret them?"
---

::: {.callout-note title="Where you are in your learning journey" icon=false}
**Where you come from.** You arrive here from [Correlation & Covariance](correlation-and-covariance.qmd) and [Probability & Sampling](probability-and-sampling.qmd). You can quantify how two variables are related (correlation), and you understand how samples vary by chance.

**What this module adds.** You'll learn what an *effect* is, how to express its size (e.g., a mean difference, Cohen's d, or r), and why 'how big is the effect?' is a different question from 'how sure are we?'.

**Why it is valuable.** Effect size answers 'how big?', while significance answers 'how sure?'. Mixing these up is one of the most common mistakes when reading research.

**Where it leads.** Next up: [Hypothesis Testing](hypothesis-testing.qmd).
:::
